answer.location_description: Small bright spot near the top of the image, slightly right of centre: rows 2-4, columns 14-16. This lies above the nodule, in surrounding lung or background, where no nodule tissue should be.
answer.mechanism: Only eight first-layer units are structured; the rest look like small-weight noise. Four negative-bias units (7, 13, 23, 29) put large positive weights on the patch. Four high-bias units (12, 14, 17, 25) put negative weights on it. In layer 2, units 7/13/23/29 feed strongly positive into u0, u1, u8, u10 and u14, whose output weights are +74, +95, +36, +50 and +94. They feed negatively into u9 (output weight -99) and u5 (-63). Units 12/14/17/25 do the opposite: they feed u9, u11, u4 and u5 (all negative output weights) and suppress u0 and u1. So a bright patch excites the malignant-side units and switches off the benign-side units. Both effects push the logit toward malignant.
answer.evidence: Positive weights on the patch: unit 7 has r3c15=54 and r4c14-16=25,26,34. Unit 29 has r3c14-16=31,53,47, r2c15-16=28,33 and r4c15=32. Unit 13 has r2c16=31, r3c16=39 and r4c16=29. Unit 23 has r2c14-16=36,26,31, r3c15=30 and r4c16=41. These are well above the surrounding top-region weights, which are mostly around ±10-20 (some rim weights are larger). Negative weights on the same spot in the benign-side units: unit 17 has r3c15=-44 and r2c16=-30. Unit 14 has r4c15-16=-30,-32. Unit 25 has r2c14-15=-20,-24, r3c15=-23 and r4c16=-20. Unit 12 has r3c14=-27 and r4c16=-24. All eight units agree on the same compact location and on a sign consistent with 'bright, therefore malignant'. That location is outside the centred nodule.
answer.main_feature: The genuine signal is the nodule's appearance in the central region versus the surrounding lung. Units 12/14/17/25 favour a compact nodule with lung around it (pushing benign). Units 7/13/23/29 respond to bright tissue extending toward the rim and an irregular margin pattern (pushing malignant).
